Title: N6945026R0026 Wharf Bravo, Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida
Awardee: ORION GOVERNMENT SERVICES LLC Houston TX 77020 USA
Description: This project is to repair and recapitalize Wharf Bravo and associated utilities at NAS Pensacola, Florida to ensure continued operational support for U.S. Coast Guard missions. The recapitalization effort will extend the service life of the wharf, improve structural integrity, and modernize utility systems to meet current operational requirements. The project includes, but is not limited to, the following major components: Structural Repairs, Mooring and Fender Systems, Wharf Hotel Services, Pavement and Drainage, and Incidental Work. Expected structural repairs include casting new concrete fascia over the existing steel combi-wall, replacing the concrete cap along the wharf, repairing holes in sheet piles, installing a galvanic cathodic protection system, and repairing and reinforcing tie-back anchors. Project includes mooring and fender systems requirements such as replacing mooring hardware and timber fender system, installing new mooring bollards, cleats, and foam-filled fenders, and each mooring bollard will include a tie-back anchor for enhanced stability. Anticipated wharf hotel services involve replacing utility systems including potable water, fire water, sanitary sewer (CHT), and electrical shore power stations. Project expected pavement and drainage requirements include removing existing pavement surfaces to access buried utilities and structural elements, repairing steel combi-wall and tie-back system, installing tie-back anchors at mooring bollards, replacing pavement with new asphalt surfaces, and constructing a stormwater drainage system with detention basin for improved runoff management. Incidental work will include all related incidental construction, demolition, and site restoration necessary to complete the recapitalization effort. Period of Performance is 548 calendar days for the Base Bid and 365 days for Option 0001.

Description: Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition, Succeeding Lease Department of Veterans Affairs Veteran Health Administration Burlington Community Based Outpatient Clinic 642GA JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 1. NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF ACTION BEING APPROVED. The Veterans Heath Administration, Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) currently leases 13,595 ABOA/14,411 Rentable Square Feet (RSF) of medical space at 3000 Lincoln Drive East, Marlton, NJ 08053 under lease number VA244-14-L-0094 for the Burlington Clinic. The current lease expired on March 3, 2026. Approval is requested to negotiate a succeeding lease with the incumbent Lessor without full and open competition for continued occupancy at this leased location. The procedures for pursuing a succeeding lease are detailed in GSAR 570.402: Succeeding Leases. 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS (INCLUDING ESTIMATED VALUE). VA submitted a continuing need letter on August 12, 2025, for 14,411 rentable square feet of clinical and related space. To satisfy the VA mission requirements the facility must be within a walkable distance of 3000 Lincoln Drive East, Marlton, NJ. This requirement is for 13,595 ABOA/14,411 RSF of space for a 15-year term to commence on March 4, 2026. The delineated area is: Northern: County Road 537 Southern: Route 70 Eastern: Pine Street/Eayrestown Rd. Western: Route 73 There is no federal space available. 3. IDENTIFICATION OF STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1): Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This statutory authority is implemented through FAR 6.103-1 (GSA Class Deviation RFO- Revised MAR 2026 2025-06) and GSAR 570.402: Succeeding Leases. In accordance with GSAR 570.402, use of the sole source authority is appropriate where the lease contracting officer does not identify any potential acceptable locations through advertisement and market research, or it is determined that award to any other offeror would result in substantial duplication of costs to the Government that are not expected to be recovered through competition. 4. DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES THE USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED. The VA Lease Contracting Officer did not identify any potential acceptable locations through the advertisement or survey of the market. Section 5 and 7 of this justification describe efforts to locate alternative sources. Therefore, in accordance with GSAR 570.402-4: No Potential Acceptable Locations, a cost benefit analysis is not required for this justification. 5. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE. Per the requirements of GSAR 570.402, the VA Lease Contracting Officer placed a sources sought/succeeding lease advertisement on the Contracting Opportunities domain of SAM.gov on June 16, 2026, for three days. In addition, market research was conducted using CoStar. 7. DESCRIPTION OF MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED AND THE RESULTS. On June 16, 2026, market research was conducted using CoStar and one (1) potentially acceptable location was identified, including the incumbent, that might meet the agency’s needs within the delineated area. In addition, the VA Lease Contracting Officer posted an advertisement conforming to GSAR 570.402-2 on the Contract Opportunities domain of SAM.gov website on June 16, 2026. See Figure 1 below for the results of the market research and SAM.gov advertisement, including the incumbent. 3000 Lincoln Drive, Marlton, NJ 08053 - Incumbent 18,353 RSF 7000 Lincoln Drive, Marlton, NJ 08053 - CoStar 20,943 RSF Revised MAR 2026 Figure 1: Market Research Comparables 8. OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. The current Lessor has demonstrated consistently strong and reliable performance throughout the term of the existing lease. All required services, including facility maintenance, building operations, security, custodial services, and timely response to service calls, have been performed in accordance with lease requirements. The Lessor has maintained an excellent record of responsiveness to government needs and has resolved any issues promptly and professionally. The building remains in good overall condition, with systems and structural components performing satisfactorily and without deficiencies that would impact mission operations. The Lessor has ensured that the space continues to meet all operational, safety, and accessibility requirements, supporting uninterrupted agency performance. Given the Government’s satisfactory experience with the current Lessor, the continued suitability of the space, and the lack of any performance issues, Lessor’s past performance supports proceeding with a succeeding lease under other than full and open competition. 9. LIST OF SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST IN THE ACQUISITION. The incumbent only. 10. STATEMENT OF ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION. There are no systemic barriers to competition. If the agency has a continuing need for space upon lease expiration, VA will follow all authorities, regulations and policies applicable to lease acquisition. Should there be remaining useful life in the Government’s tenant improvements, the Government will consider the cost of moving from the existing location, and the cost to build out new space when deciding whether to undergo a competitive action. Additionally, objective scrutiny will be given to the customer agency’s mission and security requirements, (if applicable), to eliminate unnecessary agency space requirements that may be deemed unduly restrictive.

Awardee: WHITING-TURNER CONTRACTING COMPANY, THE Baltimore MD 21286 USA
Description: The project will be to Design/Build new facilities at TRACEN Cape May, NJ. The scope of work includes but is not limited to construction of barracks buildings to accommodate an annual capacity of 5,600 recruits. It is a critical and non-negotiable requirement that the annual operational capacity of TRACEN Cape May be maintained without interruption for the entire duration of the construction project. Therefore, all construction efforts must be planned and executed in a manner that ensures no reduction in the annual number of recruits processed. The continuity of operations is a paramount objective of this project. While the RFP drawings indicate the construction of four barracks buildings, the Designer of Record is granted the flexibility to modify this number. The ultimate number of buildings is secondary to achieving the essential operational throughput. This approach allows for potential design optimizations and innovative solutions, provided the core mission-critical requirement of recruit accommodation capacity is fully satisfied. The scope of work includes but is not limited to; demolition and disposal of abandoned steam trenches, buildings and building old foundations, relocation of electrical duct banks and salvaging of transformers, temporary office trailer setup, construction of new VIP review stand, grandstands with cantilevered shading and new parade path. During construction of the new barracks a minimum of 3 barracks buildings must remain operational at all times. This project can be delivered in phases. However, the construction phases outlined here will occur only after the Base Item 0001 process is awarded and finalized. Proposed phasing is as follows: During phase 1, the existing MCPOCG (Bldg. 911) can be demolished and two temporary office trailers will be provided complete with water, sewer, electrical and C5IT connections. Two new barracks buildings can be constructed. Then James and Healy Halls can be demolished. Phase 2 will require construction of all remaining barracks facilities. In addition to the remaining barracks facilities, construction of several facilities is required in order of precedence: 1.Multi-purpose training facility (~80,000GSF) 2.Galley or expansion of existing galley to meet future throughput requirements. (~35,000GSF) 3.Fire station (~20,000GSF) The firehouse must have a natural gas generator and automatic transfer switch meeting the requirements of NFPA 70, Article 701, Legally Required Standby Systems. The generator shall be sized to power all the loads within the entire building. The UPS shall power all loads associated with emergency services. Emergency services loads include, but are not limited to: radio communication system, emergency response system, fire alarm front end, burglar alarm front end, all communication equipment, etc. Note: See Attachment H Prior to demolition of existing galley and fire station, the new facilities will need to be constructed. All facilities are required to be sustainable in accordance with the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) Guiding Principles for Federal Buildings, Dec 2020. All facilities shall strive to incorporate the best in energy efficiency, environmental performance, and advanced controls using a “whole building” integrated design approach, as well as comply with ENERGY STAR standards. The final phasing of these additional facilities will have to be determined by the Designer of Record (DOR) in coordination with the TRACEN Cape May Facility Engineering office. See site civil drawings.

Title: Prototype OTA for XVIII Airborne Corps 5G Center of Gravity Testbed
Awardee: DELL FEDERAL SYSTEMS L.P Round Rock TX 78682 USA
Description: The 419th Contracting Support Brigade, on behalf of the XVIII Airborne Corps, has awarded a sole-source Prototype Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022 to Dell Federal Systems L.P. and its primary partner, T-Mobile USA, Inc. The purpose of this Prototype OTA is to establish an experimental, secure, and resilient 100-square-mile 5G Center of Gravity Testbed at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. This research and development effort will integrate proprietary commercial carrier capabilities (T-Mobile's 5G Standalone Core) with a highly secure, experimental Private Land Mobile Network (PLMN) utilizing Dell tactical edge-compute infrastructure. The prototype focuses on validating the operational feasibility of 5G technology-as-a-service (TaaS) to support advanced mission applications for the Immediate Reaction Force (IRF), including Counter-UAS (C-UAS), real-time ISR video feeds via mandatory network slicing, and secure logistical tracking. This award was executed as a sole-source action to leverage over $31.9 million in prior joint public-private investment made under a six-year USSOCOM Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA), thereby avoiding substantial duplication of cost to the Government and preventing unacceptable operational schedule delays.

Due to the above, sole-sourcing to Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc ensures the most expedient and compliant resolution to these urgent repairs. GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(i): An urgent and compelling need exists and following the ordering procedures would result in unacceptable delays: GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii): Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized; GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iii): In the interest of economy and efficiency, the new work is a logical follow-on to an original Federal Supply Schedule order provided that the original order was placed in accordance with the applicable Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures. The original order must not have been previously issued under sole source or limited source procedures. GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(iv): It is necessary to place the order with a particular FSS contractor to satisfy a minimum guarantee established in the FSS BPA; or GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(v): A law expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified source. GSAM/R 538.7104-4: Items peculiar to one manufacturer. The required replacement equipment, system upgrades, and software enhancements for the VA Boston Healthcare System s automated prescription dispensing systems are peculiar to ScriptPro as the sole manufacturer. ScriptPro maintains exclusive proprietary rights over the system architecture, hardware components, software platforms, and all major configuration and upgrade processes necessary for continued safe and effective operation of the pharmacy automation systems currently in use. ScriptPro retains ownership of all patents associated with its robotic dispensing, storage, and vial-handling technologies, including features such as direct-to-vial dispensing, integrated labeling, barcode verification, and contamination-prevention mechanisms. These patented capabilities are not offered by any other manufacturer, and no alternate vendor can provide equipment compatible with ScriptPro s proprietary system design. Describe Why You Believe the Order Represents the Best Value consistent with GSAM/R 538.7102-2(b)(4) to aid the contracting officer in making this best value determination: The proposed order represents the best value to the Government in accordance with GSAM/R 538.7102-2(b)(4) because it ensures continuity of operations, system compatibility, and compliance with OEM exclusive technical requirements essential to maintaining safe, accurate, and efficient pharmacy services. ScriptPro systems currently in use at all three VA Boston campuses have been fully integrated with VistA and pharmacy workflows for more than 20 years, and the equipment performs critical dispensing, labeling, barcoding, inventory, and workflow management functions that directly affect patient safety and service delivery. Replacement of these end of life systems with the OEM s upgraded hardware and software ensures seamless compatibility with existing interfaces, preserves patient safety driven automation features, and prevents service disruptions that would occur if alternative systems were introduced. Price reasonableness was validated through comparison with ScriptPro s current VA Federal Supply Schedule pricing, and market research confirmed that quoted prices align exactly with the established FSS price list. However, IAW GSAM/R 538.7102-2(c)(2), further price discounts or other concessions should be sought before placing an order or establishing an FSS BPA. Only ScriptPro can perform the required OEM exclusive upgrades, including Platform to Expanded Server upgrades, GEN9 upgrades, and the WMS 2.0 transition. These upgrades are proprietary and cannot be performed by authorized distributors such as VHSS, nor by any alternative source. Selecting any vendor other than the OEM would create substantial risks of operational downtime, invalid warranty coverage, cybersecurity noncompliance, and failure of critical patient care systems. Describe the Market Research Conducted among schedule holders and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. Market research was conducted in accordance with RFO Part 10 and VAAR 810.001 70, as required for acquisitions under the Federal Supply Schedule ordering procedures referenced in GSAM/R 538.7104 3(b). The Contract Specialist performed extensive research to determine whether any sources other than ScriptPro could fulfill the VA Boston Healthcare System s requirement for replacement pharmacy automation systems and OEM exclusive system upgrades. This research included a review of historical VA acquisitions for ScriptPro equipment across multiple VISN 1 facilities, analysis of prior contract vehicles, and verification of available vendors in SAM.gov and SBA s SBS database under NAICS 339112. The search identified 983 SDVOSB/VOSB entities under the NAICS code; however, no verified firms were found that manufacture ScriptPro compatible systems or possess authorization to perform the proprietary upgrades required for continued pharmacy operations. Further review of schedule holders confirmed that ScriptPro remains the only FSS contractor capable of meeting the VABHS requirement under FSS Contract 36F79719D0135, consistent with MAS ordering authorities under 41 U.S.C. 152(3) and 40 U.S.C. 501. Direct engagement with ScriptPro representatives validated that all required upgrades including the Platform to Expanded Server upgrade, GEN9 upgrade, and Workflow Management System (WMS) 1.0 to 2.0 transition are OEM exclusive, proprietary services. ScriptPro maintains the sole rights to its system architecture, software code, firmware, robotic mechanisms, and configuration utilities, and no third party distributor (including VHSS) is authorized or qualified to perform these tasks. This proprietary limitation is reinforced by ScriptPro s active U.S. patents covering vial handling robotics, direct to vial dispensing, integrated barcode verification, and contamination prevention features capabilities not offered by any other domestic manufacturer. Because the required upgrades involve access to source controlled elements of ScriptPro s system, only the OEM can legally and technically perform the effort, meeting the criteria for limited source justification under GSAM/R 538.7104 3(b)(1)(ii) and GSAM/R 538.7104 4. Market research further demonstrated that replacing ScriptPro with an alternate automation platform would require a full divestiture of existing hardware, software, and workflow interfaces. Such a conversion would entail months of operational downtime, extensive staff retraining, revalidation of inventory workflows, reintegration with VistA and VA pharmacy systems, and acceptance testing of a new robotic dispensing architecture all of which would severely disrupt outpatient pharmacy operations. The risk is especially unacceptable given the essential nature of reliable, high volume prescription dispensing in support of direct patient care. ScriptPro s systems have been used successfully by VA Boston for over 20 years with demonstrated uptime exceeding 99% and accuracy above 99.7%, and replacing this mature ecosystem with unfamiliar technology presents significant patient safety, cyber security, warranty, and operational reliability hazards. Pricing provided by ScriptPro aligns exactly with its published VA Federal Supply Schedule price list, supporting price reasonableness under GSAM/R 538.7102 2(b)(4). The requirement was also evaluated in accordance with the hierarchy of preferences established under the Veterans First Contracting Program (VAAR 819.70), but no SDVOSB or VOSB exists that can perform the OEM exclusive upgrades or provide compatible equipment. Based on all available evidence, the results of market research conclusively demonstrate that ScriptPro is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Government s minimum needs without introducing unacceptable mission critical risk. Accordingly, the market research fully supports a sole source action to ScriptPro under FSS Contract 36F79719D0135. Any Other Facts Supporting the Justification: Additional supporting facts reinforce the need to limit consideration to ScriptPro. The existing pharmacy automation systems at the VA Boston Healthcare System have reached end of life after more than 15 years of continuous use, and failure to replace or upgrade these systems would result in significant degradation of outpatient prescription services, workflow disruptions, and increased risk to patient safety. ScriptPro equipment is fully integrated with VistA and existing pharmacy operations, and the VA Boston pharmacies rely on ScriptPro s established automation capabilities including barcode verified dispensing, real time inventory tracking, and automated vial filling and collating to maintain accuracy, efficiency, and uninterrupted prescription processing. A Statement of the Actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services is made: To reduce barriers to competition in future acquisitions, the agency will continue to monitor the automated pharmacy systems marketplace to identify whether alternative manufacturers develop solutions that are interoperable with VA pharmacy platforms or capable of meeting VA Boston s high volume, high accuracy dispensing needs. The agency will also reassess the market during future technology refresh cycles to determine whether proprietary constraints have changed or whether third party vendors gain authorization to perform upgrades, maintenance, or system modifications.

AFGSC requires development of a comprehensive, executable strategic plan aligned to its nuclear deterrence and global strike mission. The effort includes: longitudinal reassessment using prior Force Improvement Plan (FIP) analytical frameworks; integration of vitality-based constructs from the Squadron Revitalization Study; strategic alignment and gap analysis; development of strategic architecture and implementation plans; strategic launch and execution management process initiation; and transition to Government sustainment. The period of performance is 365 calendar days. Executive Leadership Group (ELG) is the only responsible source capable of satisfying this requirement without unacceptable risk to the Government. ELG led the development process and subsequent training of the initial 2014 AFGSC Force Improvement Plan (FIP) assessments and served as the architect of the analytical frameworks and structured interview methodologies used to establish AFGSC’s institutional performance baseline. ELG also conducted the Air Force Squadron Revitalization study, and designed the vitality-based analytical constructs. The current requirement is explicitly structured as a longitudinal reassessment requiring preservation of methodological continuity with the original FIP and vitality frameworks (see PWS Task 2). The Government requires: application of the original FIP analytical architecture; preservation of interpretive weighting constructs; use of vitality-based constructs embedded in prior assessments; and longitudinal comparability to prior baselines. ELG retains proprietary methodology associated with its structured interview approaches, synthesis frameworks, and integrated qualitative-quantitative analysis techniques. While the Government owns prior deliverables, the underlying analytical architecture, structured coding constructs, and interpretive sequencing logic remain ELG intellectual capital. Competition would require reconstruction or reinterpretation of analytical frameworks originally designed and applied by ELG. Such reconstruction would introduce risk of analytical distortion, degradation of longitudinal validity, and loss of comparability to prior institutional baselines. Given AFGSC’s role as the Air Force’s command for nuclear deterrence, degradation of analytical fidelity presents unacceptable mission risk. No other known source possesses direct experience architecting and applying the original FIP analytical framework, direct authorship of the vitality-based constructs used in the Squadron Revitalization study, embedded institutional knowledge necessary to preserve longitudinal validity, or demonstrated experience building strategic plans within the Department of the Air Force. Accordingly, ELG is uniquely qualified to perform this requirement. Interested vendors may submit their interest to the email address 356eceg.cons.team@us.af.mil, as the Contracting Officer may change over time. The evaluation criteria that the Air Force will utilize to determine if an interested vendor is eligible for award is as follows: The contractor shall control or otherwise have access to a quarry that can produce the aggregate required under the standards in this synopsis. The Contractor shall possess a self-certification of being a small business concern in FAR 52.212-3 - Offeror Representations and Certifications – Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The Contractor shall not possess any derogatory past performance as documented in CPARS, FAPIIS, other Government sources, and personal knowledge of Contracting Officers who have awarded contracts with that vendor in the past. The Contractor shall possess a record of either Government or private sector transactions related to the NAICS code in this synopsis. The Contractor shall meet the general standards to be considered responsible under FAR 9.104. The Contractor shall provide evidence of being capable of complying with CNMI (Marianas) import and bio-security standards if aggregate is intended to be sourced from outside the CNMI. This notice shall remain active for the duration of the Agreement's life to allow for interested vendors to submit their interest. Understand that submitting interest does not guarentee award of an Agreement.
